description: Selene Labs is a space-tech team passionate about AI,software,data,visualization, and space exploration. For NASA Space Apps 2026, we are building LUNAOPS, an interactive tool for exploring lunar landing sites,dates,terrain, Sun illumination, and Earth visibility. We are looking for teammates interested in astronomy,data science, UI/UX, 3D visualization, or scientific research who are excited to learn and build together.
summary:
LUNAOPS is an interactive lunar ops platform designed to make lunar terrain exploration and mission planning accessible and intuitive.

The platform enables you to browse an interactive 3D Moon, zoom right down into the lunar surface, place your own targets and look at the detail at a particular location. You can explore the lunar south pole, look at the changing illumination, go through the stages of a landing mission, and compare different landing sites and mission scenarios.

LUNAOPS brings lunar exploration, visualisation and mission analysis together in a single interactive workspace. Rather than just having static images and bits of information that are completely disconnected, you can actually interact with the lunar environment and get a much better sense of the challenges that are involved in planning a mission.

Our aim is to make the complex concepts behind lunar missions easier to explore, easier to understand and easier to communicate, and to support education and awareness of future lunar exploration.
details:
LUNAOPS provides an interactive environment for exploring the lunar terrain and for understanding various aspects of lunar mission planning.

The platform has an interactive lunar workspace where you can rotate and zoom in on the Moon, look at different regions of the surface and place your own lunar targets in to have a look at their details. There's also a facility for exploring the lunar south pole and a sun cycle which shows how the sunlight conditions change across the surface of the Moon.

Beyond the exploration aspects there's the full mission profile of a lunar landing mission (Earth launch, space flight, lander separation, lunar descent and touchdown). There's a mission analysis workspace where you can look at candidate landing sites, compare mission scenarios and dates and export comparison reports.

The project is designed to make lunar exploration more interactive and accessible to students, teachers, space fans and anyone who's ever wanted to know more about future lunar missions.

LUNAOPS is all about combining interactive visualisation, mission focused interfaces and data presentation into one platform. The clever bit is that it takes lunar exploration from something you just sit back and consume, and turns it into an experience that you can actually interact with.
